definitions.INNER JOIN: Rows with matches in both tables
definitions.LEFT JOIN: All left rows, plus matches from the right
definitions.RIGHT JOIN: All right rows, plus matches from the left
definitions.FULL JOIN: All rows from both tables, matched where possible
definitions.CROSS JOIN: Every row paired with every row
definitions.UNION: Stacks results of two queries; not a join
definitions.INTERSECT: Rows common to two queries; not a join
definitions.GROUP BY: Groups rows for aggregates; not a join
definitions.DISTINCT: Removes duplicate rows; not a join
definitions.LIMIT: Caps how many rows return; not a join
definitions.ORDER BY: Sorts the result; not a join
definitions.FOREIGN KEY: Links to a key in another table
definitions.DEFAULT: Value used when none is given
definitions.Candidate key: Any column set that could be the primary key
definitions.INDEX: Speeds up lookups; not a constraint
definitions.TRIGGER: Runs code on changes; not a constraint
definitions.CURSOR: Walks through rows; not a constraint
definitions.SCHEMA: Namespace for tables; not a constraint
definitions.Cassandra: Wide-column store built to scale out
definitions.CouchDB: Document database using JSON and HTTP
definitions.SQLite: Embedded relational database in one file
definitions.SAVEPOINT: Marks a point to roll back to
definitions.Isolation: Transactions don't see each other's partial work
definitions.Sharding: Splits data across servers; not a transaction term
definitions.Replication: Copies data to other servers; not a transaction term
definitions.Normalisation: Reduces redundancy; not a transaction term
definitions.CAP theorem: Distributed trade-off; not a transaction term
definitions.Index scan: Reads via an index; not a transaction term
definitions.Denormalise: Adds redundancy for speed; not a transaction term
